ratings.why: If the current person were one per server, Maya's and Theo's bots and messages would mix, breaking the stated separation.
Choosing identity only in the page lets any request read or act on another person's data, a plain breach of 'my information stays separate'.
A definite path through Setup and Continue as matters for first use, but getting the details slightly different is a smaller cost.
Any person replacing the operator's token affects everyone; a careful builder limits or explains it.
The operator needs to know which token wins and what persists, but either clear choice works if stated.
An invalid environment token hides Setup and makes every reply fail; a careful builder leads back to a fix.
The request says the token is never shown in any response, so leaking it in errors or logs is a defect.
Being able to type at once and getting a clean new bot is expected polish of the core flow.
Blank or duplicate bot names make the Bots list ambiguous, a real but contained cost.
Either keeping or rewriting the sender name on past messages is a reasonable choice of taste.
Telling conversations apart is needed to return to the right discussion, but many naming schemes serve.
Deletion of bots and conversations was not asked for.
Returning to the right bot and conversation after reload or restart is an explicit requirement.
Whether the library is per person or per bot should be decided and must never leak to another person.
Duplicate or empty names create ambiguous Use/Run/Edit/Delete buttons or silently lose text.
Renaming during Edit can silently duplicate or lose an entry, a real but smaller cost.
The person changing an instruction needs to know whether bots using it follow the change.
Viewing or clearing a bot's instructions is not asked, and 'who are you' already reveals them.
A running task is independent of its saved template, and the natural behaviour needs no special handling.
Double sends or replies attached to the wrong conversation or person are defects the request's 'not twice' rule targets.
Retry must not resend or lose the message, and a reset attempt count makes [fail once] fail forever.
Stored text should match what was typed or the choice be explained, since later answers quote it.
The stand-in's unconditional 'I've forgotten' would mislead unless the app reports honestly and avoids duplicates.
A blank memory item or an unrecoverable mistaken Forget is a real but small cost.
Correcting a memory is awkward unless the textbox starts with the current fact.
Extra transcript lines change what the stand-in counts and quotes, so the choice should be deliberate.
A person watching a long task expects progress without reloading.
Either display of finished steps is recognizable; it is presentation taste.
Applying a change to readers, id, type or owner would break the stated read rules.
Unvalidated values such as a text total or a new field pollute records, a real cost a careful builder prevents.
The request explicitly requires that reloading at an awkward moment neither loses nor double-applies a decision.
The person decides from this region, so a create should be stated exactly, including its id when stable.
Confirming a stale from-value on a shared record silently overwrites another person's change.
Two orders with the same id is a plain data defect.
Understanding what happened after a reload needs a durable outcome, but the exact form is flexible.
A confirmed change to a shared record must show in the other reader's answers or they get wrong information.
Tasks from other conversations must stay findable and cancellable, but several scopes are reasonable.
Steering targets 'the running task', so a second task's behaviour should be defined.
The stand-in claims a step was added regardless, so the app should report honestly which task got it.
A task outcome only in the Tasks region may be missed, though the request does not demand a message.
The request names an Interrupted state and recovery, so a restart mid-task must be handled honestly.
Redoing finished steps wastes work and contradicts the finished list, a real but modest cost.
The request asks for a clear account of what can still be stopped versus already happened.
Since you were away must be per person and meaningful, but its exact rule is a design choice.
Narrow use must still reach bots, conversations, memory and tasks, though how is the builder's choice.
A clear error and preserved data beat a crash or silent reset, though this is an operator edge case.
Rewriting history on forget is speculative; memory and transcript are separate by design.
The request defines Retry task for Failed and Interrupted only; extending it is taste.
A capitalized field name gets 'has no STATUS' or a bogus new-field proposal, a small but real confusion.
The stand-in answers about ORD-1001 when asked for ORD-1001A, a misleading edge a careful builder could catch.
With no stated limits, silent truncation only arises if the builder adds limits, which is speculative.
Recovering a Run after editing its saved task is a narrow edge case beyond this request.
Losing a draft typed during send reconciliation is a narrow timing edge.
Reporting an unsaved write as saved misleads, but disk failures while running are rare.
Two instances on one data folder is operator misuse outside the request.
A local no-password app can be read or driven by other sites, a real risk a careful builder blocks.
One background failure taking down the app blocks recovery of other work, a real cost to guard against.
Keyboard use is required, and focus landing on another proposal's Confirm invites mistakes.
Node already reports a port in use clearly enough for a local operator.
Errors should be shown honestly and logged so person and operator are not left guessing.
The stand-in already treats 'status of my order' as ordinary text, so it arises only if the app adds its own parsing.
